criteria.criterion: A plan is rejected by the existing gate-shape lint in .loop/run.sh — die, exit 1, before any iteration — when a task's verify names, in an inspecting position, a path that exists in HEAD and is absent from that task's files array. Inspecting covers at least grep, cat, test -f and a language-level file read such as Python open(...).read().
criteria.evidence: .loop/run.sh:313-324 (gate_inspected_paths) and :738-758 (rule 3 block) implement exactly this; T1's own verify plants and rejects grep, cat|grep, test -f && bash, and python3 -c open(...).read() forms, all of which pass when re-run (bash .loop/tests/scenarios/35-gate-unowned-file.sh and the full verify both exit 0).

criteria.criterion: The rejection line names the task id and then the offending path on the same line, in the existing '    <id>  <reason>' shape, and says why it is unpassable.
criteria.evidence: .loop/run.sh:750 — "    $id  inspects $f, which it does not own; the driver reverts that file before the gate runs, so no implementation can pass"; scenario 35 asserts assert_log 'T1 .*docs/todo.md'.

criteria.criterion: Accepted with nothing printed about gate shape: owned inspecting verify; verify that hands a HEAD file to a runner; verify reading a file absent from HEAD (durable artifact); git diff --name-only HEAD -- docs.

criteria.criterion: The rule is computed from the verify string and git's HEAD, not a filename list, and adds no per-gate/per-iteration cost — runs once in the plan phase beside the two existing rules.
